Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

The present petition has been filed by the petitioners U/s 166 & 140 M.V.Act seeking compensation of Rs. 50,00,000/- alongwith interest from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its realization being legal representatives of deceased Sunil Verma (married aged 25 years) on account of death of deceased who died in road traffic accident in question which occurred on 02.09.2018.

The petitioners also prayed for compensation MACP No. 754/18; FIR No. 206/18 DOD:12.11.2024 for irreparable monetary loss, mental agony, loss of love and affection and future prospects plus all other heads of compensation as per entitlement, caused due to accidental death of deceased.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 02.09.2018, deceased namely Sunil Verma was sitting as a pillion rider on the motorcycle which was being driven by his brother-in-law Sh. Lal.
It is averred that they were returning from Chawan Bazaar to their home at Devipur.

At around 17:45, when they reached at Bagahiya Naharpul, there was a Dumper truck bearing registration no. UP32- HN-0555, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit back of the aforesaid motorcycle, due to which deceased fell down on the road and his head got crushed under the tyre of dumper.
Deceased Sunil died at the spot and driver of motorcycle also suffered grievous injuries.
His postmortem was conducted vide PMR No. 972/2018 on 03.09.2018.
A case U/s. 279/337/304A/427 IPC was registered at PS. Atriya, UP vide FIR No. 206/18 with regard to the accident in question.
The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.1/driver.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and was duly insured with respondent no. 3/New India Assurance Co. Ltd., at the time of accident in question.

3. In their identical but separate written statement, the respondent no. 1 and 2 i.e. driver and registered owner have raised preliminary objections that alleged accident was never caused by the offending vehicle or due to the fault of respondent no. 1.
They further claimed that the respondent no. 1 was having valid driving licence at the time of accident.
Thus, insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners in the present case.
On merits, they denied the averments made in the claim petition and have prayed for its dismissal.

4. In its Written Statement, the respondent no.3 i.e. insurance company has raised preliminary objections that it is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner as there was no valid and effective permit in respect of offending vehicle at the time of accident.

It has been further claimed that insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners in case it is proved that deceased himself was negligent and solely responsible for the alleged accident and/or driver of the motorcycle on which deceased was allegedly travelling was not holding a valid and effective driving licence for the motorcycle as on the date of accident.
On merits, it has denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

5. From the pleadings of the parties and the documents, the following issues were framed vide order dated 05.09.2019:-
MACP No. 754/18; FIR No. 206/18 DOD:12.11.2024 1) Whether the deceased Sh. Sunil Verma suffered fatal injuries in road traffic accident on 02.09.2018 at about 5:45 pm AT Gram Devipur, Atariya Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh within the jurisdiction of PS. Atariya, Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh due to rashness and negligence on the part of the driver Mohd. Iliyas/R-1 who was driving vehicle bearing registration no. UP32-HN-0555, owned by Sh. Irshad Ahmed/R-2 and insured with New India Assurance Co.
Ltd./R-3?OPP.
2) Whether the LRs of deceased are entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?OPP.
3) Relief.

6. To substantiate their claim, petitioners have examined two witnesses i.e. PW1 Smt. Hasmukh Verma (mother of deceased) and PW2 Sh. Lal Soni (alleged eyewitness) and closed their evidence on 16.12.2022.
On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by any of the respondents.
7. This Tribunal has carefully perused the claim petition, evidence led by petitioners has been duly appreciated.
All documents and material relied upon perused and considered.
Arguments addressed by counsels for the petitioners and insurance company considered.
Legal position, both statutory and binding applicable precedents, has been appreciated.

The issue wise determination is as under:-

sentences.text: The onus to prove, the aforesaid issue was placed on the petitioners.

To prove the said issue,
petitioners have examined PW-2 Sh. Lal Soni (eyewitness) who deposed in her evidence that on 02.09.2018 at about 5:45 pm, he alongwith his jija ji Sh. Sunil Verma, was coming from Delhi to his home.

He further deposed that on 02.09.2018, they went to Chawan Market by the motorcycle no.
UP32-AK-6811 which was being driven by him at a normal speed and at correct side of the road and his jija ji was sitting as a pillion rider.

He further deposed that at about 7:45 pm when they reached near Bagahiya Naharpul Flyover, in the meanwhile, one dumper truck bearing registration no.
UP32-HN-0555 which was being driven rashly by its driver at a very high speed and negligently,
without taking necessary precautions and without proper lookouts, violating the traffic rules and without blowing any horn came from Neelgaon side which was going to Atariya side, hit their motorcycle with a great force, as a result of this, they both fell down on the road alongwith motorcycle and his jija ji sustained grievous and fatal injuries and his head got crushed under the tyre of dumper and he expired on the spot.
He further deposed that postmortem of deceased was conducted at Modern PM House, Sitapur, UP vide no. 972/2018.
He further deposed that he had also sustained injuries.
He categorically deposed that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving on the part of dumper truck driver.
During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance MACP No. 754/18; FIR No. 206/18 DOD:12.11.2024 company
, he deposed that he was not holding any driving licence on the date and time of accident.
He further deposed that he was driving his motorcycle on the left side of the road.
He further deposed that the offending dumper came from behind and left side of dumper had hit their motorcycle.
He further deposed that he did not remember the registration number of dumper now as he had noticed the same.
He volunteered that the dumper was apprehended at the spot.
He further deposed that the road where the accident took place was a single road.
He further deposed that he had made complaint to the police from the spot itself on the date of accident.
He volunteered that the PCR was lying halted at the spot itself.
He further deposed that neither he nor deceased was wearing helmet at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that no such accident took place with the said offending vehicle or that the said vehicle has falsely been implicated in the present case just to claim false compensation.

He denied the suggestion that accident had occurred on account of his own rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle or that he was driving his motorcycle in gross violation of traffic rules and regulations.

9. The careful perusal of testimony of aforesaid witness i.e. PW2 would go to show that the respondents more particularly insurance company has not been able to impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross- examination despite he being cross-examined at length.

It is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 206/18 u/s 279/337/304A/427 IPC was registered at PS. MACP No.
754/18; FIR No. 206/18 DOD:12.11.2024 Atariya with regard to accident in question.
Copy of said FIR (Ex. PW1/3), would show that same was registered on 02.09.2018 on the statement of aforesaid witness i.e. PW2 Sh. Lal.
The contents of said FIR would show that PW2 has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.

10. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is Chandani And Ors vs Mohd Ilyas And Ors on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147197622/
4 liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1.

11. Not only this, the respondent no. 1 namely Mohd. Iliyas (accused in State case) has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/337/304A/427 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the MACP No. 754/18; FIR No. 206/18 DOD:12.11.2024 conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

Same would also point out towards rash and negligent driving of aforesaid offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
12.
Furthermore, postmortem was got conducted on the body of deceased.
As per postmortem report (Ex. PW1/4) of deceased, cause of death of deceased was shock and hemorrhage.
All the injuries were antemortem in nature and could be possible in the manner as alleged.
The external injuries as mentioned in the relevant column correspond with the injuries which occur in Motor Vehicular Accident.
The documents filed by the petitioners have not been disputed from the side of respondents.

13. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of preponderence of probabilities that deceased Sunil Kumar had sustained fatal injuries in road accident which took place on 02.09.2018 at about 17:45 at Gram Devipur, Atariya Sitapur, UP, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
The petitioners who are claimants are the widow, minor children and father of deceased.
It is evident that the petitioners have actually suffered monetary loss and mental agony due to death of deceased.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

15. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors.,
Vs.

Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022 that: -
"The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the MV Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation'
which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or Chandani And Ors vs Mohd Ilyas And Ors on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147197622/
5 perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective MACP No. 754/18; FIR No. 206/18 DOD:12.11.2024 of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.

In Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.3, this Court has laid down as under:
"16."Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

16. The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance.

sentences.text: It is seen that the petitioners are not having any proof regarding income of deceased nor having any qualification documents, either educational or vocational, of deceased.

Thus, in the absence of any relevant document in respect of working and earning of deceased, I am of the view that income of deceased should be assessed as per the minimum wages of an unskilled person, applicable in the State of Delhi as on the date of accident.

The minimum wages of an unskilled person were Rs.
13,896/- per month as on the date of accident which is 02.09.2018.

This document has not been disproved by the respondents.
Therefore, it stands proved that date of birth of deceased is 01.01.1989 and thus, he was aged about 29 years as on the date of accident i.e.02.09.2018.

sentences.text: PW1 has categorically deposed in her evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A) that all the petitioners were financially dependent upon the income of deceased.
It is stated that the deceased was survived by five dependents i.e. widow, two children and parents of deceased.
No evidence to the contrary has been adduced by respondents.

In view of aforesaid discussions it is held that the deceased was survived by five dependents at the time of accident and hence one fourth is liable to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of deceased.
Thus, the total of loss of dependency would come out to Rs.29,76,523.20p (Rs.13,896/- X 3/4 X 140/100 X 12 X 17).
Hence, a sum of Rs. 29,77,000/-(rounded off) is awarded under this head in favour of the petitioners.

By way of pronouncement of Pranay Sethi case (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has been pleased to hold that there shall be an increase of 10% on account of 'inflation' after a period of three years.

sentences.text: Counsel for petitioner repelled the aforesaid contention on the ground that neither there was any contributory negligence on the part of driver of victim's vehicle nor any evidence has been led by insurance company in this regard.
28. As already noted above, respondent no. 3/insurance company did not adduce any evidence in this matter.
The onus to prove this plea was upon insurance company which was required to prove the same by leading cogent evidence on this issue.
However, no evidence whatsoever has been led on behalf of insurance company despite grant of opportunity.
Moreover, the testimony of eyewitness/driver of victim's vehicle clearly reveals that the offending vehicle came from behind and hit the motorcycle on which deceased was sitting as pillion rider.
Thus, there is no question for any contributory negligence on the part of driver of victim's vehicle.
Hence, the contention raised on behalf of insurance company in this regard, is hereby rejected.
29. It is nowhere the case of insurance company that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured.

Keeping in MACP No. 754/18; FIR No. 206/18 DOD:12.11.2024 view the existence of valid insurance policy and in the absence of any statutory defences available to the insurance company, respondent no. 3/insurance company concerned is legally liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.
Accordingly, issue no. 2 is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is evident that the petitioners have actually suffered monetary loss and mental agony due to death of deceased.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
Accordingly, the quantum of appropriate and adequate compensation to the victim of road accident is to be derived after assessment of various relevant parameters, as per law.
It is seen that the petitioners are not having any proof regarding income of deceased nor having any qualification documents, either educational or vocational, of deceased.
Thus, in the absence of any relevant document in respect of working and earning of deceased, I am of the view that income of deceased should be assessed as per the minimum wages of an unskilled person, applicable in the State of Delhi as on the date of accident.
Hence,
the multiplier of 17 would be applicable in view of pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as "Sarla Verma Vs. DTC" 2009 ACJ 1298 SC.
21.
In view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as, Pranay Sethi case (supra), the Tribunal considers that both the petitioners i.e. parents of deceased are entitled for payment of Rs. 40,000/- each towards "loss of consortium".
The onus to prove this plea was upon insurance company which was required to prove the same by leading cogent evidence on this issue.
However, no evidence whatsoever has been led on behalf of insurance company despite grant of opportunity.
Moreover, the testimony of eyewitness/driver of victim's vehicle clearly reveals that the offending vehicle came from behind and hit the motorcycle on which deceased was sitting as pillion rider.
Thus, there is no question for any contributory negligence on the part of driver of victim's vehicle.
